newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps firm, Brent CFDs up 8 ct, mogas $1..
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps firm, Brent CFDs up 8 ct, mogas $1..

text.p: European oil swaps were slightly firmer on Wednesday morning, extending the gentle rise that began on Tuesday afternoon.

Brent CFDs led the way, gaining 8 cents a barrel for next week's dates on the back of wet Brent trading 10 cents higher during the morning at just 82 cents under May or the equivalent of about $1 under June.
Next week's CFDs were valued around 59 cents under June by lunchtime with the following three weks at 53 cents, 47 cents and 44 cents under respectively.
The gains on Brent were reflected in firmer gasoline which is in strong demand in eastern markets.

May swaps were up about $1.50 a tonne at $195 with June trailing $2.50 lower. Crack spreads were little changed but well bid at $4.20 a barrel, $3.150, $3.45 and $4.40 on the third, fourth, first and second quarters respectively.
Heavy fuel swaps edged up 50 cents a tonne to $86.50 for May amid strong demand for physical oil in the Mediterranean.
Dealers said the deep contango remained in place and few expected much support for prompt periods.
"We might see the Med get lifted higher over the next few days but it won't last for long," said a trader.
Low sulphur remained weak with April and May holding around $90 reflecting downward pressure from good physical supply and a lack of Italian demand.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent were little changed with the third quarter valued at $4.30 a barrel and the three subsequent quarters at $4.85, $4.65 and $4.05 respectively.

Jet premiums held around $24 a tonne above the IPE for April and $25 above for May. The third quarter was $27.50 above and the fourth $33 above. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
